entities.summary:
Epigenes of Sicyon was an Ancient Greek tragic poet of the 7th century BCE, born in Argos, Greece, and died in Sicyon, Greece. He is best known for his tragic plays, which often explored the human condition and the complexities of Greek society.

His works, such as 'The Suppliants' and 'The Danaids', have had a lasting impact on Western literature, influencing later writers such as Sophocles and Euripides. Epigenes' innovative use of dramatic structure and character development helped shape the development of Greek tragedy.

Despite his significant contributions to the world of literature, Epigenes of Sicyon's life and works have been somewhat overshadowed by his namesake, the comic poet Epigenes of Sicyon, who lived in the 5th century BCE. However, recent scholarship has sought to revive Epigenes' reputation as a major figure in ancient Greek literature.

Epigenes' legacy can be seen in the enduring popularity of his plays, which continue to be performed and studied today. His influence can also be seen in the development of Western drama, from Shakespeare's 'Othello' to modern adaptations of his works.
